      "path": "src/everos/entrypoints/api/routes/memorize.py",
      "content": "\"\"\"POST /api/v2/memory/add and /api/v2/memory/flush.\n\nRoutes are thin adapters: validate the DTO (``schemas.memorize``), dump\nto dict, hand to service. No business logic lives here.\n\n``/flush`` force-closes a session's open buffer tail. The cloud edition\nexposes the same endpoint.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Annotated, Any\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Response\nfrom starlette.status import HTTP_202_ACCEPTED\n\nfrom everos.entrypoints.api.dependencies import ApplicationDep, RequestIdDep\nfrom everos.entrypoints.api.schemas import (\n    AcceptedResponseData,\n    AddResponseData,\n    FlushResponseData,\n    MemorizeAddRequest,\n    MemorizeFlushRequest,\n    SuccessEnvelope,\n)\nfrom everos.service import Queued\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/memory\", tags=[\"memory\"])\n\n\ndef _accepted(\n    response: Response, request_id: str, queued: Queued\n) -> SuccessEnvelope[AcceptedResponseData]:\n    response.status_code = HTTP_202_ACCEPTED\n    return SuccessEnvelope(\n        request_id=request_id,\n        data=AcceptedResponseData(\n            message_count=queued.message_count, pending=queued.pending\n        ),\n    )\n\n\n_ADD_RESPONSES: dict[int | str, dict[str, Any]] = {\n    202: {\n        \"model\": SuccessEnvelope[AcceptedResponseData],\n        \"description\": \"Queued: async_mode, or the session already had a backlog\",\n    },\n    413: {\"description\": \"Body over memorize.async_queue.max_payload_bytes\"},\n    429: {\"description\": \"Queue at its per-session or global cap\"},\n}\n_FLUSH_RESPONSES: dict[int | str, dict[str, Any]] = {\n    202: {\n        \"model\": SuccessEnvelope[AcceptedResponseData],\n        \"description\": \"Queued behind the session's backlog, how a flush is queued\",\n    },\n    429: {\"description\": \"Queue at its per-session or global cap\"},\n}\n\n\n@router.post(\"/add\", responses=_ADD_RESPONSES)\nasync def add_memory(\n    req: Annotated[MemorizeAddRequest, ...],\n    response: Response,\n    app: ApplicationDep,\n    request_id: RequestIdDep,\n) -> SuccessEnvelope[AddResponseData] | SuccessEnvelope[AcceptedResponseData]:\n    \"\"\"Add messages into the user-memory + agent-memory pipelines.\"\"\"\n    result = await app.memory.add(\n        req.model_dump(exclude={\"async_mode\", \"defer_extraction\"}),\n        request_id=request_id,\n        async_mode=req.async_mode,\n        defer_extraction=req.defer_extraction,\n    )\n    if isinstance(result, Queued):\n        return _accepted(response, request_id, result)\n    return SuccessEnvelope(\n        request_id=request_id,\n        data=AddResponseData(\n            message_count=result.message_count,\n            status=result.status,\n        ),\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/flush\", responses=_FLUSH_RESPONSES)\nasync def flush_memory(\n    req: Annotated[MemorizeFlushRequest, ...],\n    response: Response,\n    app: ApplicationDep,\n    request_id: RequestIdDep,\n) -> SuccessEnvelope[FlushResponseData] | SuccessEnvelope[AcceptedResponseData]:\n    \"\"\"Force boundary detection over the current ``session_id`` buffer.\n\n    Runs inline unless the session still has queued batches, in which case\n    the flush joins the queue behind them and answers 202.\n    \"\"\"\n    result = await app.memory.flush(\n        session_id=req.session_id,\n        request_id=request_id,\n        app_id=req.app_id,\n        project_id=req.project_id,\n    )\n    if isinstance(result, Queued):\n        return _accepted(response, request_id, result)\n    return SuccessEnvelope(\n        request_id=request_id,\n        data=FlushResponseData(status=result.status),\n    )\n"
    },

      "path": "src/everos/entrypoints/api/routes/search.py",
      "content": "\"\"\"POST /api/v2/memory/search — hybrid retrieval endpoint.\n\nThin adapter: validate the request DTO, dispatch to the service layer,\nreturn the envelope verbatim. ``request_id`` is generated inside the\nservice layer (uniform for OSS + cloud); we trust that value\non the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter\n\nfrom everos.entrypoints.api.dependencies import ApplicationDep\nfrom everos.service import SearchRequest, SearchResponse\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/memory\", tags=[\"memory\"])\n\n\n@router.post(\"/search\", response_model=SearchResponse)\nasync def post_search(req: SearchRequest, app: ApplicationDep) -> SearchResponse:\n    \"\"\"Hybrid retrieval across the configured memory backends.\"\"\"\n    return await app.memory.search(req)\n"
    },

      "path": "src/everos/entrypoints/api/routes/tasks.py",
      "content": "\"\"\"``GET /tasks`` -- progress of asynchronous memorize work, Cloud-shaped.\n\nThe EverOS Cloud gateway answers ``GET /api/v2/tasks/{task_id}`` and\n``GET /api/v2/tasks`` from its message bus; here the same paths read the\n``memorize_inbox`` table, so one client polls both the same way. ``task_id``\nis the ``request_id`` a ``202`` carried.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Annotated\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Query\n\nfrom everos.core.errors import NotFoundError\nfrom everos.entrypoints.api.dependencies import ApplicationDep, RequestIdDep\nfrom everos.entrypoints.api.schemas import SuccessEnvelope\nfrom everos.service import TaskItem, TaskPage\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/tasks\", tags=[\"tasks\"])\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\nasync def task_list(\n    app: ApplicationDep,\n    request_id: RequestIdDep,\n    session_id: str | None = None,\n    status: str | None = None,\n    page: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1)] = 1,\n    page_size: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1)] = 20,\n    app_id: str = \"default\",\n    project_id: str = \"default\",\n) -> SuccessEnvelope[TaskPage]:\n    \"\"\"Accepted requests, newest first; ``session_id`` / ``status`` narrow it.\n\n    Drain a session before exiting by polling with ``status=queued`` and\n    ``status=processing`` until both ``total`` are 0. ``page_size`` is capped\n    at 100.\n    \"\"\"\n    page_data = await app.ops.list_tasks(\n        session_id=session_id,\n        status=status,\n        page=page,\n        page_size=page_size,\n        app_id=app_id,\n        project_id=project_id,\n    )\n    return SuccessEnvelope(request_id=request_id, data=page_data)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{task_id}\")\nasync def task_status(\n    task_id: str,\n    app: ApplicationDep,\n    request_id: RequestIdDep,\n) -> SuccessEnvelope[TaskItem]:\n    \"\"\"One accepted request's outcome.\n\n    ``404`` once it has aged out of ``memorize.async_queue.row_retention_hours``\n    (or never existed).\n    \"\"\"\n    item = await app.ops.get_task(task_id)\n    if item is None:\n        raise NotFoundError(f\"task {task_id} not found or expired\")\n    return SuccessEnvelope(request_id=request_id, data=item)\n"

      "path": "src/everos/entrypoints/api/schemas/delete.py",
      "content": "\"\"\"Request / response DTOs of ``POST /memory/delete``.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport datetime as _dt\nimport re\nfrom typing import Literal\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator\n\nfrom .ids import (\n    PATH_SAFE_CHARSET,\n    AppScopeId,\n    PathSafeId,\n    ProjectScopeId,\n    SessionId,\n)\n\n_EPISODE_ID = re.compile(r\"(?P<owner>[a-zA-Z0-9_.@+-]{1,128})_ep_(?P<day>\\d{8})_\\d+\")\n\n\nclass DeleteRequest(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Which memories to delete: an owner, a session, or one owner's session.\n\n    At least one of ``user_id``, ``agent_id`` and ``session_id``; never both\n    ``user_id`` and ``agent_id``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n    app_id: AppScopeId = Field(\n        default=\"default\", min_length=1, max_length=128, pattern=PATH_SAFE_CHARSET\n    )\n    project_id: ProjectScopeId = Field(\n        default=\"default\", min_length=1, max_length=128, pattern=PATH_SAFE_CHARSET\n    )\n    user_id: PathSafeId | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=128)\n    agent_id: PathSafeId | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=128)\n    session_id: SessionId | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=128)\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def _one_scope(self) -> DeleteRequest:\n        if self.user_id is None and self.agent_id is None and self.session_id is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"set at least one of user_id, agent_id, session_id\")\n        if self.user_id is not None and self.agent_id is not None:\n            raise ValueError(\"user_id and agent_id are mutually exclusive\")\n        return self\n\n\nclass DeleteResponseData(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"What a deletion removed.\n\n    Attributes:\n        filters: The scope fields the request set.\n        count: Memories removed (entries, plus one per skill and one for the\n            profile when a whole owner is deleted).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    filters: list[str]\n    count: int\n\n\nclass DeleteReason(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Why the caller deletes: logged as ``code``; ``note`` is never logged.\"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n    code: Literal[\n        \"hallucination\",\n        \"outdated\",\n        \"wrong_subject\",\n        \"wrong_time\",\n        \"redundant\",\n        \"missing\",\n        \"privacy\",\n        \"style\",\n        \"other\",\n    ]\n    note: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=256)\n\n\nclass DeleteByIdsRequest(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Episodes to delete, by memory id ``<owner_id>_<entry_id>``.\n\n    The whole request is rejected (422, nothing deleted) if any id is not an\n    episode id of a path-safe owner with a real date.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n    app_id: AppScopeId = Field(\n        default=\"default\", min_length=1, max_length=128, pattern=PATH_SAFE_CHARSET\n    )\n    project_id: ProjectScopeId = Field(\n        default=\"default\", min_length=1, max_length=128, pattern=PATH_SAFE_CHARSET\n    )\n    memory_type: Literal[\"episode\"]\n    memory_ids: list[str] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=50)\n    reason: DeleteReason | None = None\n\n    @field_validator(\"memory_ids\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _episode_ids(cls, ids: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n        for memory_id in ids:\n            match = _EPISODE_ID.fullmatch(memory_id)\n            if match is None or match[\"owner\"] in (\".\", \"..\"):\n                raise ValueError(f\"not an episode memory id: {memory_id!r}\")\n            try:\n                _dt.date(\n                    int(match[\"day\"][:4]), int(match[\"day\"][4:6]), int(match[\"day\"][6:])\n                )\n            except ValueError:\n                raise ValueError(f\"no such date in {memory_id!r}\") from None\n        return list(dict.fromkeys(ids))\n\n\nclass DeleteByIdsResponseData(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"``{\"memory_type\": \"episode\", \"success\": true}`` (Cloud's shape).\"\"\"\n\n    memory_type: Literal[\"episode\"] = \"episode\"\n    success: bool = True\n"
    },

      "path": "src/everos/infra/cascade/_eraser.py",
      "content": "\"\"\"Delete a deletion's index rows at once, fenced against cascade write-backs.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\n__all__ = [\"FencedIndexEraser\"]\n\nimport asyncio\nfrom collections.abc import Collection, Mapping, Sequence\n\nfrom everos.core.observability.logging import get_logger\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.index import IndexRepositories\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.sqlite import MdChangeStateRepo\nfrom everos.memory.ports import Filter, MemoryRef, Scope, all_of, eq, one_of\n\nfrom ._fence import DeleteFence\n\nlogger = get_logger(__name__)\n\n\nclass FencedIndexEraser:\n    \"\"\":class:`~everos.memory.ports.IndexEraser` over the derived index.\n\n    Each table's delete is bounded by ``timeout_s``. A table that times out\n    or fails is logged (``memory_delete_index_erase_failed``) and every md\n    file whose rows it held is queued again, so the cascade's next run of\n    that file deletes the rows by diff. Queuing the file again is needed even\n    though rewriting it already queued it once: a run of the same file that\n    started before the rewrite may still be going, and may have read the\n    index before an even earlier run wrote the rows back.\n\n    Args:\n        index: The derived-index tables.\n        fence: Shared with the cascade projections.\n        ledger: The cascade's ``md_change_state`` queue.\n        timeout_s: Upper bound of one table's delete.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        index: IndexRepositories,\n        fence: DeleteFence,\n        ledger: MdChangeStateRepo,\n        *,\n        timeout_s: float = 15.0,\n    ) -> None:\n        self._index = index\n        self._fence = fence\n        self._ledger = ledger\n        self._timeout_s = timeout_s\n\n    async def erase(\n        self, scope: Scope, removed: Mapping[str, Sequence[MemoryRef]]\n    ) -> None:\n        self._fence.add(\n            (scope.app_id, scope.project_id, ref.id)\n            for refs in removed.values()\n            for ref in refs\n        )\n        for table, refs in removed.items():\n            if not refs:\n                continue\n            where = all_of(\n                eq(\"app_id\", scope.app_id),\n                eq(\"project_id\", scope.project_id),\n                one_of(\"id\", [ref.id for ref in refs]),\n            )\n            if not await self._delete(table, where, rows=len(refs)):\n                await self._requeue(table, {ref.md_path for ref in refs})\n\n    async def erase_owner(self, scope: Scope, kinds: Collection[str]) -> None:\n        # ponytail: no requeue on failure; the owner's files are gone, so the\n        # cascade's deletion pass over them removes the rows when it runs.\n        where = all_of(\n            eq(\"owner_id\", scope.owner_id),\n            eq(\"app_id\", scope.app_id),\n            eq(\"project_id\", scope.project_id),\n        )\n        for table in kinds:\n            await self._delete(table, where, rows=None)\n\n    async def _delete(self, table: str, where: Filter, *, rows: int | None) -> bool:\n        try:\n            async with asyncio.timeout(self._timeout_s):\n                await getattr(self._index, table).delete(where)\n        except Exception as exc:\n            logger.warning(\n                \"memory_delete_index_erase_failed\",\n                table=table,\n                rows=rows,\n                error=repr(exc)[:200],\n            )\n            return False\n        return True\n\n    async def _requeue(self, kind: str, md_paths: Collection[str]) -> None:\n        for md_path in sorted(md_paths):\n            try:\n                await self._ledger.force_enqueue(md_path, kind)\n            except Exception as exc:  # the scanner still finds the rewrite\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"memory_delete_requeue_failed\",\n                    md_path=md_path,\n                    kind=kind,\n                    error=repr(exc)[:200],\n                )\n"
    },

      "path": "src/everos/infra/cascade/_fence.py",
      "content": "\"\"\"The delete fence: index rows a deletion removed, kept from coming back.\n\nA cascade run reads an md file, embeds the entries that changed and then\nupserts them, with no lock between the read and the write. A deletion that\nrewrites the file and deletes the index rows in that gap would see its rows\nwritten back by a run that read the file before the deletion. So the\ndeletion first adds the rows' keys to this fence, then deletes them; a run\ndrops fenced rows before its upsert and checks the fence again after it,\ndeleting any row a deletion fenced meanwhile.\n\nBoth steps are synchronous, so no lock is needed: if the deletion fenced a\nrow before the run's check after the upsert, the run deletes it; if after,\nthe deletion's own delete was issued after the upsert returned.\n\nAn entry is kept only while a run that started before it is still going:\nevery run registers when it starts, before it reads the file, and\nunregisters when it ends (success, failure or timeout alike). A run that\nstarts after the deletion reads the rewritten file, which no longer has the\nentry. With no run in flight a deletion keeps nothing. A restart empties the\nfence and loses nothing: the runs in flight ended with the process.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\n__all__ = [\"DeleteFence\"]\n\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nfrom collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom everos.core.observability.logging import get_logger\nfrom everos.core.observability.metrics import Gauge\nfrom everos.memory.ports import Filter, all_of, any_of, eq, one_of\n\nlogger = get_logger(__name__)\n\ntype RowKey = tuple[str, str, str]\n\"\"\"``(app_id, project_id, id)``: the primary key of every daily-log table.\"\"\"\n\n_entries_gauge = Gauge(\n    name=\"memory_delete_fence_entries\",\n    description=\"Index rows a deletion fenced off from in-flight cascade runs.\",\n    namespace=\"everos\",\n)\n_runs_gauge = Gauge(\n    name=\"memory_delete_fence_runs\",\n    description=\"Cascade runs in flight, as registered with the delete fence.\",\n    namespace=\"everos\",\n)\n\n\nclass DeleteFence:\n    \"\"\"Row keys removed by deletions, while earlier cascade runs are in flight.\n\n    Args:\n        warn_entries: Log ``memory_delete_fence_large`` once the fence holds\n            more entries than this (``[cascade] delete_fence_warn_entries``).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, *, warn_entries: int = 100_000) -> None:\n        self._warn_entries = warn_entries\n        self._seq = 0\n        self._runs: set[int] = set()\n        self._entries: dict[RowKey, int] = {}\n        self._publish()\n\n    def register_run(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"A cascade run starts (before it reads its file); returns its token.\"\"\"\n        self._seq += 1\n        self._runs.add(self._seq)\n        self._publish()\n        return self._seq\n\n    def end_run(self, token: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"A cascade run ended, however it ended.\"\"\"\n        self._runs.discard(token)\n        self._prune()\n\n    def add(self, keys: Iterable[RowKey]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Fence the rows a deletion is about to delete from the index.\"\"\"\n        if not self._runs:\n            return  # every later run reads the rewritten file\n        self._seq += 1\n        before = len(self._entries)\n        for key in keys:\n            self._entries[key] = self._seq\n        self._prune()\n        if before <= self._warn_entries < len(self._entries):\n            logger.warning(\n                \"memory_delete_fence_large\",\n                entries=len(self._entries),\n                runs=len(self._runs),\n                threshold=self._warn_entries,\n            )\n\n    def blocks(self, row: Any) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Whether ``row`` (an index record) was fenced by a deletion.\"\"\"\n        return (row.app_id, row.project_id, row.id) in self._entries\n\n    def filter_for(self, rows: Sequence[Any]) -> Filter:\n        \"\"\"The index predicate that deletes exactly ``rows``.\"\"\"\n        ids: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)\n        for row in rows:\n            ids[(row.app_id, row.project_id)].append(row.id)\n        return any_of(\n            *(\n                all_of(eq(\"app_id\", app), eq(\"project_id\", project), one_of(\"id\", rid))\n                for (app, project), rid in ids.items()\n            )\n        )\n\n    def _prune(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drop the entries no run in flight could have read past.\"\"\"\n        oldest = min(self._runs, default=None)\n        if oldest is None:\n            self._entries.clear()\n        else:\n            self._entries = {k: s for k, s in self._entries.items() if s > oldest}\n        self._publish()\n\n    def _publish(self) -> None:\n        _entries_gauge.set(len(self._entries))\n        _runs_gauge.set(len(self._runs))\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "src/everos/infra/cascade/_projections/_daily_log_base.py",
      "content": "\"\"\"Shared diff / dispatch loop for every daily-log cascade handler.\n\nThe 4 daily-log kinds (episode / atomic_fact / foresight / agent_case)\nall do the same three-way reconcile against LanceDB:\n\n1. Parse the md into structured entries.\n2. Fetch existing rows for the same ``md_path``.\n3. ``content_sha256`` mismatch → tokenise + embed + upsert; no diff\n   → skip; row gone from md → delete.\n\nThe hash covers **only content-bearing fields** declared by each\nsubclass in :attr:`content_change_keys` (a tuple of ``\"section:Name\"``\n/ ``\"inline:name\"`` strings). Audit inline fields (owner_id /\nsession_id / timestamp / parent_id / sender_ids) are NOT in the hash\n— editing them does NOT propagate to LanceDB and does NOT waste an\nembed call.\n\nSubclasses bind their ``kind`` / ``content_change_keys`` as ClassVars,\nexpose their table's repository as ``index_repo``, and override\n:meth:`_build_row` to do the per-kind field mapping. Everything else —\nread, diff, embed call, upsert, delete — lives here.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport abc\nimport asyncio\nimport dataclasses\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\nfrom typing import Any, ClassVar\n\nfrom everos.core.observability.logging import get_logger\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.index import IndexRepository, all_of, eq, one_of\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.markdown import MarkdownReader, StructuredEntry\n\nfrom ..models import HandlerOutcome\nfrom ._common import content_sha256 as compute_content_sha256\nfrom ._common import resolve_owner, resolve_scope\nfrom .base import Handler\n\nlogger = get_logger(__name__)\n\n\n@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ParsedEntry:\n    \"\"\"One md-side entry, parsed and digested for diff.\n\n    Held immutable so the diff loop can hash / compare freely.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    entry_id: str\n    structured: StructuredEntry\n    content_sha256: str\n\n\nclass BaseDailyLogHandler(Handler):\n    \"\"\"Common chassis for the 4 daily-log cascade handlers.\n\n    Subclass requirements:\n\n    - :attr:`kind` (ClassVar[str]) — registry name, surfaces in logs.\n    - :attr:`index_repo` (property) — this kind's repository, taken from\n      ``HandlerDeps.index``.\n    - :attr:`content_change_keys` (ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]]) — the\n      subset of inline + section fields whose changes should trigger\n      re-upsert + re-embed. Each key is ``\"section:Name\"`` or\n      ``\"inline:name\"``.\n    - :meth:`_embed_texts` (override) — the texts one entry needs embedded.\n    - :meth:`_build_row` (override) — turn a :class:`ParsedEntry` plus\n      common context (owner_id / owner_type / md_path) and the vectors\n      for its texts into a typed LanceDB row. Tokenisation lives in the\n      subclass; embedding is batched here, one call per file.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    kind: ClassVar[str] = \"\"\n    content_change_keys: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ()\n\n    @property\n    @abc.abstractmethod\n    def index_repo(self) -> IndexRepository[Any]:\n        \"\"\"This kind's derived-index repository.\"\"\"\n\n    def _content_sha256(self, structured: StructuredEntry) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Hash the content-bearing subset of one entry's inline+sections.\n\n        Walks :attr:`content_change_keys`, projects each key onto its\n        ``section:`` / ``inline:`` source on the structured entry, and\n        canonicalises into a digest. Unknown key prefixes raise\n        :class:`ValueError` so a typo on a subclass surfaces immediately.\n        \"\"\"\n        parts: dict[str, str] = {}\n        for key in self.content_change_keys:\n            kind, _, name = key.partition(\":\")\n            if kind == \"section\":\n                parts[key] = structured.sections.get(name) or \"\"\n            elif kind == \"inline\":\n                parts[key] = structured.inline.get(name) or \"\"\n            else:\n                raise ValueError(\n                    f\"{type(self).__name__}.content_change_keys has unsupported \"\n                    f\"prefix in {key!r}; expected 'section:' or 'inline:'\"\n                )\n        return compute_content_sha256(parts)\n\n    async def handle_added_or_modified(self, md_path: str) -> HandlerOutcome:\n        # Registered before the file is read, ended however the run ends:\n        # a deletion that fences rows while this run is going keeps them out\n        # of this run's upsert (``_apply_lance_changes``).\n        fence = self._deps.fence\n        token = fence.register_run() if fence is not None else None\n        try:\n            return await self._project(md_path)\n        finally:\n            if fence is not None and token is not None:\n                fence.end_run(token)\n\n    async def _project(self, md_path: str) -> HandlerOutcome:\n        absolute = self._deps.memory_root.root / md_path\n        parsed = await MarkdownReader.read(absolute)\n        new_entries = [\n            ParsedEntry(\n                entry_id=entry.id,\n                structured=entry.as_structured(),\n                content_sha256=self._content_sha256(entry.as_structured()),\n            )\n            for entry in parsed.entries\n        ]\n\n        existing = await self.index_repo.find_where(\n            eq(\"md_path\", md_path),\n            limit=10_000,\n            skip_vectors=True,\n        )\n        owner_id, owner_type = resolve_owner(parsed.frontmatter, md_path)\n        app_id, project_id = resolve_scope(md_path)\n\n        to_build, skipped = self._diff_entries(new_entries, existing)\n        to_upsert = await self._embed_entries(\n            to_build,\n            owner_id,\n            owner_type,\n            app_id,\n            project_id,\n            md_path,\n        )\n        # Rows a memory deletion fenced while this run was going stay out.\n        fence = self._deps.fence\n        if fence is not None:\n            to_upsert = [row for row in to_upsert if not fence.blocks(row)]\n        new_by_id = {e.entry_id for e in new_entries}\n        to_delete_ids = [\n            row.entry_id for row in existing if row.entry_id not in new_by_id\n        ]\n\n        await self._apply_lance_changes(to_upsert, to_delete_ids, md_path)\n        await self._propagate_deprecations(\n            parsed.frontmatter,\n            owner_id,\n            app_id,\n            project_id,\n        )\n        return HandlerOutcome(\n            md_path=md_path,\n            kind=self.kind,\n            upserted=len(to_upsert),\n            deleted=len(to_delete_ids),\n            skipped=skipped,\n        )\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _diff_entries(\n        new_entries: list[ParsedEntry],\n        existing: list[Any],\n    ) -> tuple[list[ParsedEntry], int]:\n        \"\"\"Compare new entries against existing rows, return changed + skip count.\"\"\"\n        existing_by_entry = {row.entry_id: row for row in existing}\n        to_build: list[ParsedEntry] = []\n        skipped = 0\n        for entry in new_entries:\n            prior = existing_by_entry.get(entry.entry_id)\n            if prior is not None and prior.content_sha256 == entry.content_sha256:\n                skipped += 1\n                continue\n            to_build.append(entry)\n        return to_build, skipped\n\n    async def _embed_entries(\n        self,\n        to_build: list[ParsedEntry],\n        owner_id: str,\n        owner_type: str,\n        app_id: str,\n        project_id: str,\n        md_path: str,\n    ) -> list[Any]:\n        \"\"\"Build LanceDB rows for changed entries.\n\n        Every text the changed entries need goes out in ONE ``embed_batch``\n        call (the provider chunks it by ``batch_size``), not one ``embed``\n        call per entry: the per-entry fan-out queued N single-input requests\n        on the process-wide embedding semaphore ahead of the interactive\n        query embedding (issue #486).\n        \"\"\"\n        if not to_build:\n            return []\n        texts_per_entry = [self._embed_texts(entry) for entry in to_build]\n        flat = [text for texts in texts_per_entry for text in texts]\n        vectors: Sequence[list[float] | None]\n        embedding = self._deps.embedding\n        if embedding is None:\n            logger.debug(\n                \"cascade_handler_embed_skipped\",\n                kind=self.kind,\n                md_path=md_path,\n                entries=len(to_build),\n                reason=\"embedding_capability_unavailable\",\n            )\n            vectors = [None] * len(flat)\n        else:\n            vectors = [list(v) for v in await embedding.embed_batch(flat)]\n        rows: list[Any] = []\n        cursor = 0\n        for entry, texts in zip(to_build, texts_per_entry, strict=True):\n            entry_vectors = vectors[cursor : cursor + len(texts)]\n            cursor += len(texts)\n            rows.append(\n                await self._build_row(\n                    owner_id=owner_id,\n                    owner_type=owner_type,\n                    app_id=app_id,\n                    project_id=project_id,\n                    md_path=md_path,\n                    entry=entry,\n                    vectors=entry_vectors,\n                )\n            )\n        return rows\n\n    async def _apply_lance_changes(\n        self,\n        to_upsert: list[Any],\n        to_delete_ids: list[str],\n        md_path: str,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Flush upserts and deletes to LanceDB.\n\n        The fence is checked again once the upsert returned: a deletion that\n        fenced a row after this run filtered it relied on this run to delete\n        it (the two share no lock).\n        \"\"\"\n        fence = self._deps.fence\n        if to_upsert:\n            await self.index_repo.upsert(to_upsert)\n            late = [r for r in to_upsert if fence.blocks(r)] if fence else []\n            if late:\n                await self.index_repo.delete(fence.filter_for(late))\n        if to_delete_ids:\n            await self.index_repo.delete(\n                all_of(eq(\"md_path\", md_path), one_of(\"entry_id\", to_delete_ids))\n            )\n\n    async def handle_deleted(self, md_path: str) -> HandlerOutcome:\n        deleted = await self.index_repo.delete_by_md_path(md_path)\n        return HandlerOutcome(\n            md_path=md_path,\n            kind=self.kind,\n            upserted=0,\n            deleted=deleted,\n            skipped=0,\n        )\n\n    async def _propagate_deprecations(\n        self,\n        frontmatter: Any,\n        owner_id: str,\n        app_id: str,\n        project_id: str,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Propagate deprecated_entries from frontmatter to LanceDB.\n\n        The md file is the source of truth; cascade reconstructs the\n        ``deprecated_by`` column on every sync/rebuild.\n        \"\"\"\n        deprecated = \"\"\"LanceDB table name, resolved from :attr:`schema.TABLE_NAME`.\"\"\"\n        return self.schema.TABLE_NAME\n\n    @classmethod\n    def _write_lock(cls, table_name: str) -> asyncio.Lock:\n        \"\"\"Return the write lock for ``table_name``; create on first use.\n\n        ``dict.setdefault`` is atomic under single-threaded asyncio (no\n        ``await`` between check and insert), so no meta-lock is needed.\n        \"\"\"\n        return cls._table_locks.setdefault(table_name, asyncio.Lock())\n\n    @asynccontextmanager\n    async def _deadline(self, budget: float, op: str) -> AsyncIterator[None]:\n        \"\"\"Bound an operation that does **not** take the write lock.\n\n        Same last-resort guarantee as :meth:`_locked` minus the lock: the\n        maintenance scheduler runs one task per kind and skips a kind whose\n        task has not finished, so any await in that path which can hang must\n        have a deadline or that kind stops being maintained for good.\n        \"\"\"\n        try:\n            async with asyncio.timeout(budget):\n                yield\n        except TimeoutError as exc:\n            logger.warning(\n                \"lancedb_operation_deadline_exceeded\",\n                table=self.table_name,\n                op=op,\n                budget_seconds=budget,\n            )\n            raise VectorStoreBusyError(\n                f\"{op} on table {self.table_name!r} exceeded its {budget:g}s deadline\"\n            ) from exc\n        except RuntimeError as exc:\n            if not _is_transient_execution_error(exc):\n                raise\n            logger.warning(\n                \"lancedb_transient_execution_error\",\n                table=self.table_name,\n                op=op,\n                error=str(exc)[:200],\n            )\n            raise VectorStoreBusyError(\n                f\"{op} on table {self.table_name!r} hit a transient lance \"\n                f\"execution error: {exc}\"\n            ) from exc\n\n    @asynccontextmanager\n    async def _locked(self, budget: float, op: str) -> AsyncIterator[None]:\n        \"\"\"Hold the table write lock for at most ``budget`` seconds.\n\n        **The deadline covers acquisition *and* the body.** That is the whole\n        point: every critical section on this lock is bounded, so no code path\n        can wait for it — or hold it — indefinitely. A single stuck operation\n        would otherwise wedge the table forever, because a stuck holder blocks\n        every writer *and* the maintenance scheduler skips a kind whose task\n        never finishes (observed in a soak run: one table stopped reclaiming\n        versions permanently, 150 versions retained, disk 11x live size, with\n        no error logged anywhere because nothing failed — it simply never\n        returned).\n\n        On expiry the body is cancelled, the lock is released, and the timeout\n        is re-raised as :class:`VectorStoreBusyError` so the cascade worker\n        treats it as transient and retries instead of marking the row\n        permanently failed.\n\n        Callers resolve the table handle **inside** this block, not before it.\n        Resolving it outside leaves an unbounded await ahead of the deadline,\n        and a maintenance task that hangs there never returns — which silently\n        parks that kind forever, because the scheduler skips a kind whose task\n        is still in flight (observed in a soak run: one table stopped pruning\n        for 13 minutes with zero failure logs while its siblings pruned fine).\n        \"\"\"\n        started = time.monotonic()\n        acquired_at: float | None = None\n        try:\n            async with asyncio.timeout(budget):\n                with LOCKS.observe(\"lance_table\", self.table_name):\n                    async with self._write_lock(self.table_name):\n                        acquired_at = time.monotonic()\n                        yield\n        except TimeoutError as exc:\n            # ``acquired`` is the load-bearing field: it separates \"never got\n            # the lock\" (a holder is slow or stuck) from \"got it and overran\"\n            # (this operation itself is slow), which is exactly what a soak\n            # investigation cannot otherwise tell apart.\n            now = time.monotonic()\n            logger.warning(\n                \"lancedb_write_lock_deadline_exceeded\",\n                table=self.table_name,\n                op=op,\n                budget_seconds=budget,\n                acquired=acquired_at is not None,\n                waited_seconds=round((acquired_at or now) - started, 3),\n                held_seconds=round(now - acquired_at, 3) if acquired_at else 0.0,\n            )\n            raise VectorStoreBusyError(\n                f\"{op} on table {self.table_name!r} exceeded its \"\n                f\"{budget:g}s write-lock deadline\"\n            ) from exc\n        except RuntimeError as exc:\n            # The soak's spill failures came out of ``merge_insert`` (this\n            # path), not the reads: worker -> upsert -> execute_merge_insert.\n            # The write is idempotent by id, so a retry is the right answer.\n            if not _is_transient_execution_error(exc):\n                raise\n            logger.warning(\n                \"lancedb_transient_execution_error\",\n                table=self.table_name,\n                op=op,\n                error=str(exc)[:200],\n            )\n            raise VectorStoreBusyError(\n                f\"{op} on table {self.table_name!r} hit a transient lance \"\n                f\"execution error: {exc}\"\n            ) from exc\n        else:\n            held = time.monotonic() - (acquired_at or started)\n            if held >= _SLOW_HOLD_LOG_SECONDS:\n                logger.info(\n                    \"lancedb_write_lock_slow_hold\",\n                    table=self.table_name,\n                    op=op,\n                    held_seconds=round(held, 3),\n                    waited_seconds=round((acquired_at or started) - started, 3),\n                )\n\n    @classmethod\n    def _reset_locks_for_tests(cls) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test-only: drop the write-lock pool.\n\n        ``asyncio.Lock`` binds to the current event loop on first\n        ``acquire()``; pytest-asyncio creates a fresh loop per test, so\n        a module-level lock surviving across tests fails with \"bound to\n        a different event loop\". The production cascade worker runs on\n        one loop forever and does not need this hook. Mirrors\n        :func:`everos.memory._partition_locks._reset_for_tests`.\n        \"\"\"\n        cls._table_locks.clear()\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        table: AsyncTable | None = None,\n        *,\n        source: TableSource | None = None,\n        dim: int,\n        timeouts: LanceTimeouts = LanceTimeouts(),  # noqa: B008 - frozen value\n        sweep_husks: HuskSweep | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        if (table is None) == (source is None):\n            raise TypeError(\n                f\"{type(self).__name__}: pass exactly one of table / source\"\n            )\n        self._table_override = table\n        self._source = source\n        self._vector_dim = dim\n        self._timeouts = timeouts\n        self._sweep_husks: HuskSweep = sweep_husks or remove_empty_index_dirs\n\n    @cached_property\n    def index_schema(self) -> IndexSchema:\n        \"\"\"The record's neutral schema at this repo's vector width.\n\n        Lazy so a record with no ``PRIMARY_KEY`` is refused by the write path\n        (``upsert``) with its own message rather than at construction.\n        \"\"\"\n        return schema_for(self.schema, dim=self._vector_dim)\n\n    @cached_property\n    def arrow_schema(self) -> pa.Schema:\n        \"\"\"The Arrow schema the table is created and written with.\"\"\"\n        return arrow_schema_for(self.index_schema)\n\n    async def _table(self) -> AsyncTable:\n        if self._table_override is not None:\n            return self._table_override\n        assert self._source is not None\n        return await self._source.table(self.schema.TABLE_NAME, self.arrow_schema)\n\n    def _to_arrow(self, records: Sequence[T]) -> pa.Table:\n        self._check_vector_widths(records)\n        return pa.Table.from_pylist(\n            [record.model_dump() for record in records], schema=self.arrow_schema\n        )\n\n    def _check_vector_widths(self, records: Sequence[T]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Refuse a vector whose length is not the configured width.\n\n        The records carry no width, so this is where a wrong-width embedding\n        is caught. Arrow would refuse it too, but as an anonymous\n        ``ArrowInvalid`` the cascade can only record as a failed write; a\n        width mismatch is configuration, so it is named as such.\n\n        Raises:\n            IndexSchemaMismatchError: A vector's length differs from the\n                column's width.\n        \"\"\"\n        for field in self.index_schema.vector_fields:\n            for record in records:\n                vector = getattr(record, field.name)\n                if vector is not None and len(vector) != field.dimension:\n                    raise IndexSchemaMismatchError(\n                        f\"table {self.table_name!r} column {field.name!r} expects \"\n                        f\"vectors of width {field.dimension} ([embedding] dim) but \"\n                        f\"got {len(vector)}; the embedding model and dim disagree\"\n                    )\n\n    # ── Create ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    async def add(self, records: Sequence[T]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Insert one or more records.\"\"\"\n        async with self._locked(self._timeouts.write, \"add\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            await table.add(self._to_arrow(records))\n\n    # ── Upsert ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    async def upsert(self, records: Sequence[T]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Merge ``records`` into the table on ``schema.PRIMARY_KEY``.\n\n        Invariant: every write to a business table is a merge on its\n        declared primary key. ``merge_insert(on=...)`` is the only\n        uniqueness LanceDB offers — a key match replaces the row wholesale,\n        no match inserts — so as long as this is the sole write path, two\n        rows with one key cannot come into existence. There is no ``by``\n        parameter on purpose: the key is the table's declaration, not the\n        caller's choice.\n\n        Cascade uses this when reconciling md → LanceDB: an entry seen\n        for the first time inserts; an entry that was edited in md\n        updates its existing row.\n        \"\"\"\n        key = getattr(self.schema, \"PRIMARY_KEY\", None)\n        if not key:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"derived-index model {self.schema.__name__} has no PRIMARY_KEY\"\n            )\n        async with self._locked(self._timeouts.write, \"upsert\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            await (\n                table.merge_insert(list(key))\n                .when_matched_update_all()\n                .when_not_matched_insert_all()\n                .execute(self._to_arrow(records))\n            )\n\n    # ── Maintenance ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    async def optimize(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Compact fragments + merge new data into the FTS / vector indexes.\n\n        ``optimize()`` is a **performance + storage-hygiene** operation,\n        **not** a correctness/visibility one. LanceDB's ``merge_insert``\n        writes new data into a fresh fragment that the FTS / vector\n        indexes don't cover yet; queries stay correct regardless because\n        LanceDB transparently brute-force flat-scans that unindexed tail\n        and unions it with the indexed hits. Verified on lancedb 0.30.2:\n        after ``create_index`` + ``merge_insert`` (no ``optimize()``), a\n        ``nearest_to_text`` for a token present only in the new rows\n        returns those rows immediately.\n\n        (Older lancedb — at/below the ``>=0.13.0`` floor this repo once\n        pinned — did **not** flat-scan the FTS tail, so post-build rows\n        were genuinely invisible to BM25 until ``optimize()``; that is\n        the behaviour the historical LoCoMo-conv0 note described. The\n        flat-scan fallback closed that gap, so optimize is now purely\n        about keeping that tail small.)\n\n        What ``optimize()`` actually buys on the current stack:\n\n        - **Query speed** — the unindexed tail is flat-scanned on every\n          query; merging it into the index keeps that scan bounded as\n          ingest accumulates.\n        - **Storage hygiene** is *not* done here — physical reclamation\n          of replaced fragments / stale manifests / dead index files is\n          :meth:`prune`, a separate write-locked call.\n\n        Cascade triggers this through a per-kind throttle + trailing\n        edge scheduler (``IndexMaintainer.schedule_optimize``): at most\n        one run per throttle window per kind, decoupled from the drain\n        loop, with a 60s heartbeat sweep as a safety net. Cost is\n        O(N) data-rewrite per optimized fragment; the throttle is how\n        we cap it under sustained write pressure. Because visibility no\n        longer depends on it, the throttle window can be generous.\n\n        This is **compaction only** — physical reclamation of superseded\n        files is :meth:`prune`, a separate write-locked call. Kept lock-free\n        on purpose: a ``Retryable commit conflict`` against a concurrent\n        writer is benign here (compaction is not urgent — the next scheduled\n        beat retries), so it must not stall writers.\n        \"\"\"\n        async with self._deadline(self._timeouts.compact, \"optimize\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            await table.optimize()\n\n    async def prune(self, older_than: dt.timedelta) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Physically reclaim files from versions older than ``older_than``.\n\n        LanceDB's ``AsyncTable`` cannot clean up independently of compaction —\n        the only handle is ``optimize(cleanup_older_than=..., delete_unverified=...)``,\n        which bundles compact + cleanup into one manifest commit. Under\n        sustained churn that commit is a Rewrite that concurrent Delete /\n        Update writes preempt, so the bundled cleanup loses the race and\n        never runs (observed in the storage soak: 16 successes / 547 conflicts\n        over 21h → the index dir grew unbounded to the disk guardrail).\n\n        Fix: run it **under the per-table write lock** so no write is in\n        flight for its duration. That does two things at once:\n\n        1. **No commit conflict** — the Rewrite has the manifest to itself,\n           so cleanup actually completes every beat.\n        2. **Cross-process safe** — ``delete_unverified=False`` keeps lance\n           from deleting any file it cannot tie to a removed version, i.e. a\n           file a writer in *another process* (a CLI ``cascade sync`` /\n           ``backfill``) may be mid-commit on. The per-table write lock is\n           in-process only, so it cannot fence a second process; the flag is\n           what makes concurrent processes safe. Measured to reclaim\n           identically to ``delete_unverified=True`` on churned tables (both\n           collapse superseded versions ~97%), because ordinary churn\n           orphans are all version-referenced and therefore verifiable —\n           ``True`` only additionally deletes in-flight / dangling files,\n           which is exactly the corruption vector. Reclaiming *during* active\n           load comes from running under the write lock so the cleanup commit\n           never loses the manifest race, not from the flag.\n\n        ``cleanup_older_than`` deletes the *files* under a\n        superseded ``_indices/<uuid>/`` but never the directory (lance's\n        ``cleanup.rs`` contains no directory removal at all — it is written\n        against an object store where an empty directory does not exist), so\n        those husks accumulate on a local filesystem: a soak run reached 13061\n        dirs, 98% empty. They are swept here, outside the lock — see\n        :func:`remove_empty_index_dirs` for why that is safe.\n\n        This is a *separate* gap from index files not being reclaimed while\n        they are young: lance skips an index UUID that no manifest references\n        until it is 7 days old, and a short retention window deletes those\n        manifests first, so the files lose their last reference and wait out\n        the full 7 days (measured: 260MB retained on a 19k-row soak table,\n        reclaimed in full once backdated past the threshold).\n\n        The trade-off is a brief write stall (~seconds on a churned table,\n        dominated by the cleanup's file scan/delete — flat, not proportional\n        to the backlog). Cascade runs it on a slow beat\n        (``CascadeWorker._optimize_prune_interval``, default 300s), so the\n        stall is rare. Does *not* shrink **active** index internals (FTS\n        ``part_N`` / index UUID count) — that is ``rebuild_indexes``'s job.\n        \"\"\"\n        async with self._locked(self._timeouts.prune, \"prune\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            await table.optimize(cleanup_older_than=older_than, delete_unverified=False)\n            table_uri = await table.uri()\n            live_uuids = frozenset(\n                i.index_uuid for i in await table.list_indices() if i.index_uuid\n            )\n        # Lock-free: the sweep can only ``rmdir``, which the kernel refuses on a\n        # non-empty directory, so it cannot lose data no matter who else is\n        # writing. Keeping it out of the critical section also means a slow\n        # filesystem walk cannot overrun the prune budget.\n        #\n        # Best-effort means best-effort: the cleanup commit above already\n        # succeeded, so a sweep timeout must not escape ``prune()``. Letting it\n        # escape bills the failure to the wrong account — the optimize\n        # scheduler counts a prune \"failure\" (feeding the fallback-rebuild\n        # threshold) and the prune-staleness clock stops advancing, both\n        # reporting a cleanup stall that did not happen. Same defect shape as\n        # the alert counter the fallback rebuild used to zero: an auxiliary\n        # path corrupting the main signal's ledger. The skipped husks are\n        # retried on the next heavy beat.\n        try:\n            async with self._deadline(self._timeouts.husk_sweep, \"prune_husk_sweep\"):\n                removed = await asyncio.to_thread(\n                    self._sweep_husks,\n                    table_uri,\n                    live_uuids=live_uuids,\n                    min_age_seconds=_HUSK_MIN_AGE_SECONDS,\n                )\n        except VectorStoreBusyError:\n            # _deadline already logged lancedb_operation_deadline_exceeded.\n            removed = 0\n        if removed:\n            logger.debug(\n                \"lancedb_pruned_empty_index_dirs\",\n                table=self.table_name,\n                removed=removed,\n            )\n\n    async def rebuild_indexes(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drop and re-create every index on this table.\n\n        **Why this exists** — workaround for an upstream Python API gap:\n\n        Lance's Rust ``OptimizeOptions`` has a ``num_indices_to_merge``\n        knob (default 1) that bounds the number of active index UUIDs\n        per column. With ``Some(1)``, every ``optimize_indices()`` call\n        merges its delta into the base — active UUID count stays at 1.\n\n        Two problems block us from using it from the application layer:\n\n        1. ``lancedb.AsyncTable.optimize()`` does **not expose** this\n           parameter (verified on lancedb main 2026-05-28). It forwards\n           only ``cleanup_since_ms`` and ``delete_unverified`` to Rust.\n        2. Even calling Lance directly via ``pylance``, the merge\n           behaviour itself is buggy on ``lance crate 4.0`` (what\n           lancedb 0.30.2 embeds) — ``num_indices_to_merge=1`` does\n           nothing. Fix landed in ``lance 7.x``, but ``pylance 7.x``\n           can not collapse indexes on a ``lance 4.0``-format dataset\n           (verified by experiment).\n\n        So in our current stack there is **no application-level path**\n        to bound active index UUID growth. ``optimize()`` keeps\n        accumulating one new UUID (vector) / one new ``part_N`` (FTS)\n        per call.\n\n        This method is the workaround: rebuild every indexed column from the\n        schema's declarations (:mod:`.indexes`). Measured effect — the live\n        index goes from 7 files back to 4 after 25 ``optimize()`` beats, i.e.\n        the fragment set does collapse. The rebuild is an **O(N) full retrain**\n        but cheap in practice (~0.3s for 50k rows × 2 FTS columns on local SSD).\n\n        It rebuilds **in place** (``create_index(replace=True)``) rather than\n        dropping first. An earlier version dropped every index and recreated\n        them, on the assumption that LanceDB falls back to a brute-force scan\n        meanwhile. That is true for vector search and **false for FTS**: with no\n        inverted index a BM25 query raises ``Cannot perform full text search\n        unless an INVERTED index has been created`` (measured). Because the\n        recall legs are gathered without ``return_exceptions``, one failing leg\n        fails the whole search request, so the window was a source of 500s.\n\n        **Cadence** — :class:`CascadeWorker` runs this on a slow loop\n        (default 12h per kind). Frequency is bounded by the rebuild\n        cost, not by correctness — even daily is fine functionally;\n        12h is a conservative pick to keep file/UUID counts well below\n        any FD ceiling under steady-state ingest.\n\n        **When to remove** — once lancedb exposes ``num_indices_to_merge``\n        on the async Python API **and** the embedded ``lance crate``\n        ships the working merge implementation, delete this method and\n        switch to ``optimize(num_indices_to_merge=1)`` in the regular\n        ``optimize()`` path. Tracking issues / context:\n\n        - https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/issues/2193\n        - https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/issues/3177\n        - https://github.com/lance-format/lance/pull/6711 (partial fix\n          in lance v7.0.0)\n        - https://docs.rs/lancedb/latest/lancedb/table/struct.OptimizeOptions.html\n        \"\"\"\n        async with self._locked(self._timeouts.rebuild, \"rebuild_indexes\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            # Replace in place rather than drop-then-create. The live columns\n            # must never be left without an index: FTS does not degrade when\n            # its index is missing the way vector search does — it raises\n            # ``Cannot perform full text search unless an INVERTED index has\n            # been created``, and the recall legs are gathered without\n            # ``return_exceptions``, so the whole search request 500s. Only\n            # indexes on columns that are no longer indexed at all get dropped;\n            # nothing queries those, so their drop opens no window.\n            wanted = set(self.index_schema.bm25_fields) | {\n                field.name for field in self.index_schema.vector_fields\n            }\n            for idx in await table.list_indices():\n                if not wanted.intersection(idx.columns or ()):\n                    await table.drop_index(idx.name)\n            await indexes.ensure_fts_indexes(table, self.index_schema, replace=True)\n            await indexes.ensure_vector_indexes(\n                table, self.index_schema, min_rows=_vector_index_min_rows()\n            )\n\n    # ── Read ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    async def ensure_vector_indexes(self) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Build the ANN index on vector columns that crossed the row\n        threshold since startup, and retrain one whose delta indices piled\n        up — the cascade's heavy beat calls this; the cases are spelled out\n        on :func:`.indexes.ensure_vector_indexes`.\"\"\"\n        async with self._locked(self._timeouts.rebuild, \"ensure_vector_indexes\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            return await indexes.ensure_vector_indexes(\n                table, self.index_schema, min_rows=_vector_index_min_rows()\n            )\n\n    async def count(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Total row count.\"\"\"\n        async with self._deadline(self._timeouts.read, \"count\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            return await table.count_rows()\n\n    async def get_by_id(\n        self,\n        id_value: str,\n        *,\n        id_field: str = \"id\",\n    ) -> T | None:\n        \"\"\"Fetch one row by scalar PK; ``None`` if missing.\n\n        Uses LanceDB scalar filter ``<id_field> = '<id_value>'``. Single\n        quotes in ``id_value`` are doubled to avoid breaking the SQL-like\n        predicate; everos's PK convention is ``<owner_id>_<entry_id>``\n        which never contains quotes, so the escape is defensive.\n        \"\"\"\n        async with self._deadline(self._timeouts.read, \"get_by_id\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            rows = (\n                await table.query()\n                .where(f\"{id_field} = '{_q(id_value)}'\")\n                .limit(1)\n                .to_list()\n            )\n        if not rows:\n            return None\n        return self.schema.model_validate(rows[0])\n\n    async def find_where(\n        self,\n        where: str,\n        *,\n        limit: int = 100,\n        skip_vectors: bool = False,\n    ) -> list[T]:\n        \"\"\"Scalar query returning *typed* schema instances.\n\n        Like :meth:`search` but returns ``list[T]`` rather than raw\n        LanceDB row dicts. No vector ANN; pure scalar filter only.\n        Use :meth:`search` when you need ``_distance`` or want to mix\n        ANN with filters.\n\n        ``skip_vectors``: leave the vector columns out of the\n        read; they come back as ``None``. Each 1024-D vector becomes 1024\n        Python floats in ``to_list``, so bulk readers that never use them\n        should set this.\n        \"\"\"\n        async with self._deadline(self._timeouts.read, \"find_where\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            query = table.query().where(where)\n            if skip_vectors:\n                query = query.select(\n                    [\n                        f.name\n                        for f in self.index_schema.fields\n                        if f.kind is not IndexFieldKind.DENSE_VECTOR\n                    ]\n                )\n            rows = await query.limit(limit).to_list()\n        return [self.schema.model_validate(r) for r in rows]\n\n    async def find_one_where(self, where: str) -> T | None:\n        \"\"\"Single-row variant of :meth:`find_where` (``None`` if no match).\"\"\"\n        rows = await self.find_where(where, limit=1)\n        return rows[0] if rows else None\n\n    async def find_where_paginated(\n        self,\n        where: str,\n        *,\n        sort_by: str,\n        descending: bool = True,\n        page: int = 1,\n        page_size: int = 20,\n        max_fetch: int = 20000,\n    ) -> tuple[list[T], int]:\n        \"\"\"Paginated scalar query with in-memory sort.\n\n        LanceDB has no native ``ORDER BY``. The chassis fetches up to\n        ``max_fetch`` rows matching ``where``, sorts the resulting Arrow\n        table by ``sort_by``, then slices ``page`` × ``page_size``. The\n        *true* row count of the predicate is returned alongside the\n        page so callers can render pagination controls without a second\n        query.\n\n        Args:\n            where: SQL-like scalar predicate. Required (no implicit\n                full-table scan from ``find_where_paginated``).\n            sort_by: Column name to sort the result set by.\n            descending: ``True`` (default) → newest first; ``False`` →\n                ascending.\n            page: 1-indexed page number.\n            page_size: Rows per page.\n            max_fetch: Cap on rows pulled before the in-memory sort.\n                When the predicate matches more rows than this cap the\n                page is sorted over an *arbitrary* prefix and the page\n                contents are only approximately correct — the chassis\n                emits a warning so the caller learns about the\n                truncation.\n\n        Returns:\n            ``(rows, total)`` — ``rows`` is the typed page,\n            ``total`` is ``count_rows(filter=where)`` (the predicate's\n            true match count, regardless of ``max_fetch``).\n        \"\"\"\n        async with self._deadline(self._timeouts.read, \"find_where_paginated\"):\n            table = await self._table()\n            total = await table.count_rows(filter=where)\n            if total > max_fetch:\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"find_where_paginated truncated\",\n                    extra={\n                        \"table\": self.table_name,\n                        \"where\": where,\n                        \"total\": total,\n                        \"max_fetch\": max_fetch,\n                    },\n                )\n            arrow_tbl = await table.query().where(where).limit(max_fetch).to_arrow()\n        order = \"descending\" if descending else \"ascending\"\n        arrow_tbl = arrow_tbl.sort_by([(sort_by, order)])\n        offset = (page -       "content": "\"\"\"Base business writer for daily-log markdown files.\n\nDaily-log files (memcell / episode / case / atomic_fact / foresight)\nshare three things:\n\n    * scope (user-track or agent-track, derived from the schema)\n    * filename pattern: ``<FILE_PREFIX>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`` under\n      ``<scope_root>/<scope_id>/<DIR_NAME>/``\n    * entry id pattern: ``<ENTRY_ID_PREFIX>_<YYYYMMDD>_<NNN>``\n\n:class:`BaseDailyWriter` factors out **path resolution + entry-id\nconstruction + today's date default**, leaving frontmatter field\nmaintenance (e.g. ``entry_count`` / ``last_appended_at``) to concrete\nbusiness subclasses.\n\nSubclass usage::\n\n    class _MemcellWriter(BaseDailyWriter):\n        schema = UserMemcellDailyFrontmatter\n\n    writer = _MemcellWriter(layout)\n    eid = writer.append(\"u_jason\", body=\"...\")\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport datetime as _dt\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Collection, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, ClassVar\n\nimport anyio\n\nfrom everos.core.observability.logging import get_logger\nfrom everos.core.utils.datetime import today_with_timezone\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.markdown._base.entries import (\n    Entry,\n    EntryId,\n    render_structured_entry,\n    split_entries,\n)\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.markdown._base.frontmatter import (\n    BaseFrontmatter,\n    parse_frontmatter,\n)\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.markdown._base.reader import MarkdownReader\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.markdown._base.writer import MarkdownWriter\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.memory_root import MemoryRoot\n\nlogger = get_logger(__name__)\n\n\nclass BaseDailyWriter:\n    \"\"\"Append a new entry to today's (or a given date's) daily-log file.\n\n    Subclasses bind a single :class:`BaseFrontmatter` subclass via the\n    ``schema`` ClassVar. Callers passing\nmore ``memcell_ids`` than this fan out into multiple SELECTs, merged\nin-memory — see the direct-path selector in\n``memory/strategies/extract_user_profile.py`` where\n``last_profile_ts=0`` can pull an owner's entire episode history.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass MemcellRepo(RepoBase[Memcell]):\n    model = Memcell\n\n    async def insert_many(self, rows: list[Memcell]) -> list[Memcell]:\n        \"\"\"Insert MemCell rows in one transaction; rows are constructed by caller.\"\"\"\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            s.add_all(rows)\n            await s.commit()\n            for r in rows:\n                await s.refresh(r)\n        return rows\n\n    async def find_by_ids(self, memcell_ids: list[str]) -> list[Memcell]:\n        \"\"\"Bulk fetch rows by primary key list — preserves caller order.\n\n        Chunked at ``_SQLITE_IN_CHUNK`` to protect against\n        ``SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER`` blowups on large owner histories\n        (e.g. ``extract_user_profile``'s direct path when ``user.md``\n        doesn't exist yet — ``last_profile_ts=0`` fetches every memcell\n        the owner has ever produced).\n\n        Used by offline strategies that pull every memcell in a cluster\n        (membership lives in :class:`ClusterMember` and is supplied to\n        the strategy via :class:`everalgo.clustering.Cluster.members`).\n        \"\"\"\n        if not memcell_ids:\n            return []\n        by_id: dict[str, Memcell] = {}\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            for start in range(0, len(memcell_ids), _SQLITE_IN_CHUNK):\n                chunk = memcell_ids[start : start + _SQLITE_IN_CHUNK]\n                stmt = select(Memcell).where(Memcell.memcell_id.in_(chunk))\n                rows = (await s.execute(stmt)).scalars().all()\n                by_id.update((r.memcell_id, r) for r in rows)\n        return [by_id[mid] for mid in memcell_ids if mid in by_id]\n\n    async def mark_case_extracted(\n        self,\n        memcell_id: str,\n        *,\n        extracted_at: dt.datetime,\n        skip_reason: str | None,\n        skip_detail_json: str | None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Stamp the agent-case extraction outcome;       "content": "\"\"\"Repository for ``memorize_inbox`` — the async memorize queue.\n\nBound to the session factory it is built with.\n\nExposes the queue primitives the worker and the route need:\n\n- :meth:`claim_next` — smallest-id ``queued`` row outside the sessions in\n  flight, flipped to ``processing``.\n- :meth:`mark` — land a row in a new status (attempt / error bookkeeping).\n- :meth:`count_pending` — cap checks (one session, or all).\n- :meth:`requeue_processing` — startup crash recovery.\n- :meth:`fail_abandoned` — the stuck-row sweep.\n- :meth:`purge_expired` — retention sweep.\n- :meth:`list_tasks` — ``GET /tasks`` (filter by session / status, paged).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport datetime as dt\nfrom collections.abc import Collection\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import delete, func, select, update\n\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.sqlite._base.repository import RepoBase\nfrom everos.infra.persistence.sqlite._base.session import session_scope\nfrom everos.memory.ports import LOST_STATUS_WRITE, REPLAYS_EXHAUSTED_PREFIX\n\nfrom .._tables import MemorizeInbox\n\nPENDING_STATUSES: tuple[str, ...] = (\"queued\", \"processing\")\n\n\ndef replays_exhausted(n: int) -> str:\n    return f\"{REPLAYS_EXHAUSTED_PREFIX}{n} times without finishing; giving up\"\n\n\n# Joins (app_id, project_id, session_id) into one comparable key in SQL.\n_SCOPE_SEP = \"\\x1f\"\n\n\nclass MemorizeInboxRepo(RepoBase[MemorizeInbox]):\n    model = MemorizeInbox\n\n    async def claim_next(\n        self, *, exclude_sessions: Collection[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> MemorizeInbox | None:\n        \"\"\"Flip the smallest-id ``queued`` row to ``processing`` and return it.\n\n        ``exclude_sessions`` are ``(app_id, project_id, session_id)`` scopes\n        that already have a row in flight; their queued rows are skipped so a\n        session never runs two batches at once and keeps its arrival order.\n        \"\"\"\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            stmt = (\n                select(MemorizeInbox)\n                .where(MemorizeInbox.status == \"queued\")\n                .order_by(MemorizeInbox.id.asc())  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n                .limit(1)\n            )\n            if exclude_sessions:\n                scope_key = (\n                    MemorizeInbox.app_id  # type: ignore[operator]\n                    + _SCOPE_SEP\n                    + MemorizeInbox.project_id\n                    + _SCOPE_SEP\n                    + MemorizeInbox.session_id\n                )\n                stmt = stmt.where(\n                    scope_key.not_in([_SCOPE_SEP.join(k) for k in exclude_sessions])\n                )\n            row = (await s.execute(stmt)).scalars().first()\n            if row is None:\n                return None\n            row.status = \"processing\"\n            await s.commit()\n            await s.refresh(row)\n            return row\n\n    async def mark(\n        self,\n        row_id: int,\n        *,\n        status: str,\n        attempt: int | None = None,\n        last_error: str | None = None,\n        payload_json: str | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Set ``status`` (and optionally ``attempt`` / ``last_error`` /\n        ``payload_json``) on one row. A delivered row passes ``payload_json=\"\"``\n        so the request body does not sit on disk for the retention period.\n        \"\"\"\n        values: dict[str, object] = {\"status\": status}\n      values[\"payload_json\"] = payload_json\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            await s.execute(\n                update(MemorizeInbox).where(MemorizeInbox.id == row_id).values(**values)\n            )\n            await s.commit()\n\n    async def count_pending(\n        self,\n        *,\n        session_id: str | None = None,\n        app_id: str = \"default\",\n        project_id: str = \"default\",\n    ) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Rows still ``queued`` or ``processing``: one session's, or all.\"\"\"\n        where = [MemorizeInbox.status.in_(PENDING_STATUSES)]  # type: ignore[attr-defined]\n        if session_id is not None:\n            where += [\n                MemorizeInbox.app_id == app_id,\n                MemorizeInbox.project_id == project_id,\n                MemorizeInbox.session_id == session_id,\n            ]\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            stmt = select(func.count()).select_from(MemorizeInbox).where(*where)\n            return int((await s.execute(stmt)).scalar_one())\n\n    async def fail_abandoned(self, *, exclude_ids: Collection[int] = ()) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Mark every ``processing`` row outside ``exclude_ids`` as ``failed``.\n\n        The worker passes the rows it is running; any other ``processing``\n        row lost its status write and its outcome is unknown.\n        \"\"\"\n        stmt = (\n            update(MemorizeInbox)\n            .where(MemorizeInbox.status == \"processing\")\n            .values(status=\"failed\", last_error=LOST_STATUS_WRITE)\n        )\n        if exclude_ids:\n            stmt = stmt.where(MemorizeInbox.id.not_in(list(exclude_ids)))  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            result = await s.execute(stmt)\n            await s.commit()\n            return int(result.rowcount or 0)\n\n    async def requeue_processing(self, *, max_replays: int = 3) -> tuple[int, int]:\n        \"\"\"Startup recovery: return ``processing`` rows to ``queued``, bounded.\n\n        A row left ``processing`` was in flight when the process died; it is\n        delivered again (at-least-once) and ``attempt`` counts that replay.\n        A row already replayed ``max_replays`` times is marked ``failed``\n        instead, so a batch that kills the process cannot crash-loop it.\n        Returns ``(requeued, given_up)``.\n        \"\"\"\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            gave_up = await s.execute(\n                update(MemorizeInbox)\n                .where(\n                    MemorizeInbox.status == \"processing\",\n                    MemorizeInbox.attempt >= max_replays,\n                )\n                .values(status=\"failed\", last_error=replays_exhausted(max_replays))\n            )\n            requeued = await s.execute(\n                update(MemorizeInbox)\n                .where(MemorizeInbox.status == \"processing\")\n                .values(status=\"queued\", attempt=MemorizeInbox.attempt + 1)\n            )\n            await s.commit()\n            return int(requeued.rowcount or 0), int(gave_up.rowcount or 0)\n\n    async def count_status(self, status: str) -> int:\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            stmt = (\n                select(func.count())\n                .select_from(MemorizeInbox)\n                .where(MemorizeInbox.status == status)\n            )\n            return int((await s.execute(stmt)).scalar_one())\n\n    async def oldest_pending_created_at(self) -> dt.datetime | None:\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            stmt = select(func.min(MemorizeInbox.created_at)).where(\n                MemorizeInbox.status.in_(PENDING_STATUSES)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]\n            )\n            return (await s.execute(stmt)).scalar_one()\n\n    async def list_tasks(\n        self,\n        *,\n        session_id: str | None = None,\n        status: str | None = None,\n        app_id: str = \"default\",\n        project_id: str = \"default\",\n        offset: int = 0,\n        limit: int = 20,\n    ) -> tuple[list[MemorizeInbox], int]:\n        \"\"\"Rows for ``GET /tasks``: newest first, plus the unpaged total.\n\n        ``session_id`` (with its ``app_id`` / ``project_id`` scope) and\n        ``status`` narrow the listing; either may be omitted.\n        \"\"\"\n        where = []\n        if session_id is not None:\n            where += [\n                MemorizeInbox.app_id == app_id,\n                MemorizeInbox.project_id == project_id,\n                MemorizeInbox.session_id == session_id,\n            ]\n        if status is not None:\n            where.append(MemorizeInbox.status == status)\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            total = (\n                await s.execute(\n                    select(func.count()).select_from(MemorizeInbox).where(*where)\n                )\n            ).scalar_one()\n            rows = (\n                (\n                    await s.execute(\n                        select(MemorizeInbox)\n                        .where(*where)\n                        .order_by(MemorizeInbox.id.desc())  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n                        .offset(offset)\n                        .limit(limit)\n                    )\n                )\n                .scalars()\n                .all()\n            )\n        return list(rows), int(total)\n\n    async def purge_expired(self, *, before: dt.datetime) -> tuple[int, int]:\n        \"\"\"Delete rows created before ``before`` unless still ``processing``.\n\n        Two plain DELETEs rather than one with ``RETURNING`` (SQLite < 3.35\n        has no ``RETURNING``). Only the worker changes ``queued`` rows and the\n        sweep runs inside it, so the split is exact. Returns\n        ``(deleted, deleted_queued)``; a non-zero second value means rows\n        aged out without ever being delivered (the worker was down).\n        \"\"\"\n        expired = MemorizeInbox.created_at < before\n        async with session_scope(self._factory) as s:\n            undelivered = await s.execute(\n                delete(MemorizeInbox).where(expired, MemorizeInbox.status == \"queued\")\n            )\n            terminal = await s.execute(\n                delete(MemorizeInbox).where(\n                    expired,\n                    MemorizeInbox.status.in_((\"success\", \"failed\")),  # type: ignore[attr-defined]\n                )\n            )\n            await s.commit()\n            queued = int(undelivered.rowcount or 0)\n            return queued + int(terminal.rowcount or 0), queued\n"
    },
